Tabelog: 長崎堂 心斎橋本店 (Nagasaki Do Shinsaibashi honten), Japanese sweets / café / Western sweets, Shinsaibashi-suji 2-1-29, Chuo-ku, Osaka, about 2 min on foot from Shinsaibashi Station exit 6, Mon, Tue and Thu–Sun 10:00–17:30, closed Wednesday, reservations accepted, cards, e-money and QR-code payments accepted, 10 seats, non-smoking, wheelchair accessible, children welcome, takeout. Official site: founded 1919 (Taisho 8); castella above all, plus Crystal Bonbon, 虹のかけら (Rainbow Fragments), dorayaki and Waffel. The founder 荒木源四郎 opened the confectionery 扇正軒 in Dejima, Nagasaki; moved to Osaka in 1924 as 合資会社長崎堂; patent for canned castella in 1934; in 1951 the second-generation head 敏夫 hung the sign 「本舗 長崎堂」 in 周防町 (now Shinsaibashi-suji 2-1-29); the canned castella was taken as rations by an Annapurna climbing expedition; in 1960 it became 株式会社大阪長崎堂 under the third-generation head 荒木一郎; around 1973 the head shop's music box was bought; Crystal Bonbon launched around 1980; in 1981 the writer 田辺聖子 visited the head shop, which appears in 「苺をつぶしながら」; the restored castella in 1982; the red-rice sweet 赤米寿 sold only on the 1st and 15th of the month; in 2003 the fourth-generation head 荒木貴史 became representative director; in 2013 the Shinsaibashi head shop was renewed with 「1919長崎堂」; centenary in 2019. Shops: the Shinsaibashi head shop and the Sumiyoshi shop, plus supermarkets and souvenir outlets (Kansai Airport, Itami Airport, Shin-Osaka Station and others). Chairman and representative director 荒木貴史. Group-company page: the Nagasaki Do group is the parent of three brands, Nagasaki Do, QUOLOFUNE (head shop in Jiyugaoka, Tokyo) and Zen Kashoin (Muromachi, Kyoto). Reviews (March 2025 – October 2026): the head-shop set ¥1,100 (Crystal Bonbon, Rainbow Fragments, castella or the red-rice sweet, coffee or a pot of tea); Crystal Bonbon ¥2,160, two per person; a line before opening; chestnut dorayaki ¥183–184; an iced dorayaki set; pudding à la mode; sakura castella; an Expo-character castella; Waffel; moist castella with coarse sugar on the base; a big music box you can play with a special coin; kind staff; one diner found the bonbons and castella ordinary.

Official site: Italian Sweets Ruggeri, Nambanaka 2-chome 8-93, Naniwa-ku, Osaka; 11:00–19:00 (closing at 19:00 from 1 October 2026); closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Always 13–16 kinds of gelato; a Solo can be taken home; dry ice available; premium gelato costs ¥50 or more extra. Recipes balanced to taste better than the ingredient itself; fruit ripened and the recipe matched to its sugar level; about −13 °C gives authentic smoothness, so eat it in the shop first. Premium: シチリアピスタチオ (Sicilian pistachio from Bronte, the most popular), チョコラートビオンド (blond chocolate), マンドルラート (almond), ティラミスドルチェ (tiramisu), メープルゴルゴンゾーラ (maple and gorgonzola).
